overall: Atlanta is sitting at 82.4°F as of 10:00 AM ET with a brisk warming velocity of +5.4°F/hr, indicating active daytime heating is underway. The running max has been flat since 06:55, suggesting the real climb is just beginning. With a dewpoint of 69.8°F, moisture is elevated and could modestly cap peak heating, but conditions overall are tracking toward a hot afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: Three of four NWP models (GFS at 89.9, HRRR at 89.9, ECMWF at 89.2) show tight clustering in the upper 80s to near 90°F, while NBM comes in lower at 87.5°F — a notable outlier. The high-confidence even ensemble (Tier 1) reinforces the upper range at 90–91°F, while the odd ensemble (Tier 4, Avoid) pointing to 87–88°F carries very little weight given its low probability and poor tier rating.
max_temp_prediction: The preponderance of evidence — three major models near 89.2–89.9°F plus the Tier 1 even ensemble flagging 90–91°F — strongly suggests today's high will land in the 89–90°F range. The elevated dewpoint and NBM's lower 87.5°F forecast introduce some downside risk, but the dominant signal is for a near-90°F peak. Confidence is moderately high; the primary uncertainty is whether boundary-layer moisture will limit the final push above 90°F.
